title: A Contact for the Cover
premise: Bram Delacroix, a financial-crimes investigator who launders reputations for the powerful, notices that a private flight's records have been erased mid-air — and realizes they were meant to be on it. Pulled into a conspiracy where an attack is being staged as an accident to bury evidence of corruption at the highest levels, Bram must trace the money backward through memory, forged ledgers, and their own compromised past. The trail leads to the mentor who taught Bram that clean money is just well-told fiction. In the end, Bram exposes the plot but chooses exile over credit, paying the price of survival: erasing themselves the way the flight was erased.
about_author: Ivo Eastwick is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside the quiet machinery of international finance before leaving to write. They live off-grid in coastal Portugal and refuse interviews about their previous career.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Bram Delacroix's POV. We meet them mid-case, scrubbing a shipping magnate's ledger until his fortune reads like virtue. Bram is competent, numb, and quietly haunted by how good they've become at making guilt invisible. Emotional beat: hollow professionalism masking a hunger for something real.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine audit flags an anomaly: every record of Flight 447-V vanishes while radar still tracks it airborne. Bram pulls the thread against orders. The beat is cold dread — the system that pays them has begun deleting reality itself.

chapters.title: Attribution Denied
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Their supervisor, Vess, orders the anomaly buried; no one wants this case attributed. Bram copies the fragments anyway. Beat: first act of rebellion, small and irreversible, laced with fear of what obedience would cost instead.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest, Redacted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Mara Quist, a disgraced air-traffic controller who logged the flight's final transmissions. She heard something before the signal died. Beat: two strangers realize they're holding halves of the same erased truth.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following money trails, Bram finds shell companies funding the flight — and a payment routed to themselves three years ago, from an account they don't recognize. Beat: vertigo; the conspiracy may have authored Bram's own survival.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding flight-path data, she finds a pattern of 'accidents' scheduled months apart, each erasing a witness or a document. One date remains open: eleven days out. Beat: rising urgency — this isn't history, it's a schedule.

chapters.title: Vess Knows
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Confronting Vess, Bram gets a warning wrapped in kindness: some cases are load-bearing; pull them and the building comes down on you. Beat: betrayal and temptation — Vess offers Bram a promotion built on silence.

chapters.title: Ghost Account
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Tracing the mysterious payment, Bram reaches a dead fixer's storage unit: files on dozens of people whose lives were 'cleaned' — including Bram's own file, annotated in handwriting they know intimately. Beat: gut-punch recognition.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me Fiction
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Bram's POV. Years earlier: Aldous Renner, legendary investigator and Bram's mentor, teaching that every fortune is a story someone agreed to believe. Present-day Bram realizes the handwriting is Renner's. Beat: grief braided with dawning horror.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara identifies the target of the staged accident: a whistleblower's testimony hearing, timed so the crash destroys both the witness and the evidence chain. Beat: the stakes crystallize into human terms — a nervous accountant named Osei who knows everything.

chapters.title: Recruiting a Ghost
chapters.summary: Bram and Mara's alternating POV. They find Osei hiding in plain sight and try to convince him the hearing is a trap. He doesn't trust them; Bram shows him their own redacted file. Beat: fragile alliance formed from mutual damage.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Trail
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. To move Osei safely, Bram manufactures a false money trail — using their darkest skills for protection instead of concealment. Beat: redemption flickers; the corrupted gift turned briefly toward light.

chapters.title: Renner Calls
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Renner contacts Bram directly, warm and terrible, offering full absolution if Bram delivers Osei — or Mara. He frames it as mercy: everyone survives if the story ends on schedule. Beat: seduction of power; Bram wavers at the edge.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers what 'survival' means in Renner's economy: witnesses who cooperated live on as erased versions of themselves — new names, hollowed lives. Beat: moral clarity hardens; survival without self is another word for death.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram plays double agent, feeding Renner a fabricated location for Osei while the real plan moves. Every message is a knife balanced on its tip. Beat: peak tension, Bram performing the role they were trained for one last time.

chapters.title: Signal Lost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The trap half-works: Renner's team intercepts the decoy, but Mara is taken in the confusion, her comms cut. Beat: devastating cost — the plan's success is indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With hours left, Bram trades their entire case archive — years of leverage over the powerful — to locate Mara. Beat: sacrifice; Bram burns their armor to save a person, choosing humanity over safety.

chapters.title: The Hearing Room
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. Inside the hearing, Osei testifies as the 'accident' is armed above — a chartered aircraft with failing systems, timed to the minute. Beat: claustrophobic countdown; ordinary courage under impossible pressure.

chapters.title: Grounding the Ghost
chapters.summary: Bram and Mara's alternating POV. Rescued Mara reroutes the aircraft's clearance while Bram forces the flight's true records into the public record mid-session. The attack collapses into visibility. Beat: triumphant reversal, breathless and costly.

chapters.title: Renner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Final confrontation with Renner, who offers Bram succession: the empire of clean stories, with Bram as author. Bram refuses — and publishes Renner's own file, unredacting the man who made them. Beat: climax resolved not by violence but by refusing inheritance.

chapters.title: Attribution Accepted
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Testimony, fallout, hearings. Bram could claim credit and be restored — but restoration means reabsorption into the machine. Instead Bram signs the deposition under their own name once, then walks away from the institution entirely. Beat: bittersweet liberation.

chapters.title: A Contact for the Cover
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mara's POV. Months later, Mara receives a postcard with no return address: coordinates to a coastal town, and a single line — 'some records should stay deleted.' She smiles, deletes her own copy of Bram's file, and lets the sea keep the secret. Beat: quiet resolution; memory as the one archive no one can launder.
